content:
The image shows a person scouting a soybean field with widespread yellowing throughout the canopy. The leaves appear yellow-green to yellow across the entire visible field, suggesting a broad foliar chlorosis event. No close-up lesion details are visible, but the uniform canopy-wide yellowing at what appears to be a vegetative-to-reproductive stage is the key feature.

Key observations:
- Widespread, diffuse yellowing across the full field canopy
- Uniform distribution (not patchy like SCN tends to be)
- Plants in the mid-to-late season stage
- Person examining individual plants, consistent with scouting for a foliar or systemic disease

The widespread interveinal-type yellowing pattern across the full canopy is most consistent with **Sudden Death Syndrome**, which causes scattered yellow spots between veins that expand into large chlorotic/necrotic blotches, with the whole field appearing yellow-green from a distance. SDS is one of the most common causes of this field-level presentation. Brown Stem Rot is a differential, but BSR typically shows more distinct interveinal necrosis with brown pith when stems are split.
